# Pet Import Regulations — China

## Overview
China has strict pet import requirements. All dogs and cats entering China must meet microchip, vaccination, titer test, and health certificate requirements. Quarantine on arrival is mandatory.

## Required Documents
- Microchip certificate
- Rabies vaccination record
- Rabies titer test result (from approved laboratory)
- Official health certificate endorsed by national authority
- Import permit (in some cases — check with destination city authority)

## Microchip Requirements
- Standard: ISO 11784/11785
- The microchip must be implanted before any vaccinations are administered
- If the microchip is implanted after the first rabies vaccination, the vaccination series must be restarted

## Vaccination Requirements
- Rabies vaccination is mandatory for all dogs and cats
- The vaccination must be administered after microchip implantation
- First-time (primary) vaccinations must be given at least 30 days before the date of travel
- The vaccination must be valid — not expired — at time of entry
- Typical validity: 1 year for annual vaccines, 3 years for triennial vaccines (check your specific product)

## Rabies Titer Test
- A rabies antibody titer test is required for all dogs and cats entering China
- Blood sample must be drawn at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination
- The result must show an antibody level of at least 0.5 IU/ml
- The test must be performed at a laboratory approved by the Chinese authorities
- The titer test result must be presented alongside the health certificate

## Health Certificate
- Must be issued by an accredited (official) veterinarian
- Must be issued within 10 days of the travel date
- Must be endorsed/stamped by the national competent authority (e.g. USDA APHIS in the US, APHA in the UK, BVET in Germany)
- The certificate must list: microchip number, vaccination dates, titer test result, owner details, and destination

## Quarantine Rules
- All dogs and cats entering China are subject to mandatory quarantine inspection at the port of entry
- Standard quarantine period: 7 days at a government-designated quarantine facility
- The quarantine period can be extended up to 30 days if documentation is incomplete or the animal shows signs of illness
- The owner is responsible for all quarantine costs (facility fees, veterinary inspections)
- Owners cannot stay with their pet during quarantine

## Approved Entry Ports
- Not all international airports in China accept imported pets
- Approved entry ports include: Beijing Capital International Airport, Shanghai Pudong International Airport, Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport
- Always confirm with your airline and the Chinese customs authority before booking

## Breed Restrictions
- Certain dog breeds are subject to restrictions or bans in major Chinese cities
- Beijing bans dogs with a shoulder height above 35cm in urban districts
- Check the specific regulations for your destination city before travel

## Airline Policies
Airline pet policies vary widely and are separate from government import regulations — both must be satisfied.
- **Air China**: Does not allow pets in the cabin on international flights. Pets must travel as checked baggage or air cargo, in an IATA-approved travel crate.

- **Lufthansa**: Allows small dogs and cats in the cabin (in an IATA-approved carrier under the seat) on flights to China, subject to a combined pet + carrier weight limit (typically around 8 kg). Larger pets travel as checked baggage.
- **China Eastern / China Southern**: Generally do not allow pets in the cabin on international routes; pets travel as checked baggage or cargo, similar to Air China.
- Always confirm the current cabin/cargo policy, carrier size limits, and any advance booking requirements directly with the airline — policies can change and may differ by route.

## Important Warnings
- Start the process at least 3–4 months before travel — the titer test alone requires 30 days after vaccination, plus lab processing time
- Health certificates expire quickly (10-day window) — book your vet appointment as close to departure as possible
- Always verify current requirements with the Chinese embassy or consulate in your country, as regulations can change

## Sources
- General Customs Administration of the People's Republic of China (GACC)
- Chinese embassy/consulate official guidance

# Pet Import Regulations — Germany

## Overview
Germany follows EU pet travel rules. Dogs, cats, and ferrets entering Germany must have a valid EU pet passport, a microchip, and an up-to-date rabies vaccination. Dogs may also require tapeworm treatment depending on their country of origin. No quarantine is required for compliant pets.

## Required Documents
- EU pet passport (mandatory for dogs, cats, and ferrets)
- Microchip certificate (recorded in the passport)
- Rabies vaccination record (recorded in the passport)
- Tapeworm treatment record (dogs only, depending on origin country)

## Microchip Requirements
- Standard: ISO 11784/11785
- The microchip must be implanted before or at the same time as the first rabies vaccination
- If the microchip is implanted after the first rabies vaccination, the vaccination must be repeated after the microchip is in place

## EU Pet Passport
- All dogs, cats, and ferrets entering Germany must have a valid EU pet passport
- The passport must be issued by an authorised veterinarian in an EU member state
- It must contain: microchip number, owner details, vaccination records, and treatment records
- Pets from non-EU countries require a third-country equivalent document that meets EU standards

## Vaccination Requirements
- Rabies vaccination is mandatory
- The primary vaccination is only valid after a 21-day waiting period from the date of administration
- Booster vaccinations must be given before the previous vaccination expires
- Typical validity: 1 year or 3 years depending on the vaccine product used
- The vaccination date and expiry must be recorded in the EU pet passport

## Tapeworm Treatment (Dogs Only)
- Required for dogs entering Germany from certain non-EU countries and some EU countries with specific risk profiles
- Must be administered between 1 and 5 days before arrival in Germany
- The active ingredient must be praziquantel (minimum 50mg) or equivalent
- The treatment date, product name, and veterinarian's signature must be recorded in the pet passport
- Dogs travelling only within the EU (e.g. from France to Germany) are generally exempt, but check the specific origin country

## Quarantine Rules
- No quarantine is required for pets entering with a valid EU pet passport and complete documentation
- Pets from high-risk rabies countries may be subject to additional checks at the border

## Age Restrictions
- Puppies and kittens must be at least 15 weeks old to enter Germany
- This is calculated as: 12 weeks minimum age for primary vaccination + 21-day waiting period
- Younger animals cannot be legally imported, even with documentation

## Non-EU Pets
- Pets from non-EU countries must meet additional requirements
- A rabies antibody titer test may be required depending on the origin country's risk classification
- The titer test must show a result of at least 0.5 IU/ml
- A 3-month waiting period after a successful titer test may apply for high-risk countries

## Airline Policies
Airline pet policies vary widely and are separate from government import regulations — both must be satisfied.
- **Lufthansa**: Allows small dogs and cats in the cabin (in an IATA-approved carrier under the seat) on most flights to/from Germany, subject to a combined pet + carrier weight limit (typically around 8 kg). Larger pets travel as checked baggage.

- **Air China**: Does not allow pets in the cabin on flights between Germany and China. Pets must travel as checked baggage or air cargo.
- **Turkish Airlines**: Allows small pets in the cabin on flights between Germany and Turkey, subject to carrier size and weight limits.
- Always confirm the current cabin/cargo policy, carrier size limits, and any advance booking requirements directly with the airline — policies can change and may differ by route.

## Important Warnings
- The 21-day waiting period after primary rabies vaccination is mandatory — a pet vaccinated the day before travel is not compliant
- Always check whether your origin country requires tapeworm treatment before entry into Germany
- Puppies born during relocation must be at least 15 weeks old before they can travel

## Sources
- European Commission pet travel rules (EU Regulation 576/2013)
- German Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture (BMEL)
- German customs authority (Zoll)

# Pet Import Regulations — Turkey

## Overview
Turkey's pet import rules are broadly aligned with EU standards. Dogs and cats with complete documentation — microchip, valid rabies vaccination, and an official health certificate — can enter without quarantine. EU pet passports are accepted for EU residents.

## Required Documents
- Microchip certificate
- Rabies vaccination record
- Official health certificate (or EU pet passport for EU residents)
- Tapeworm treatment record (dogs only)

## Microchip Requirements
- Standard: ISO 11784/11785
- The microchip must be implanted before the rabies vaccination is administered
- If the microchip is implanted after vaccination, the vaccination series must be restarted from the beginning

## Vaccination Requirements
- Rabies vaccination is mandatory for all dogs and cats
- The vaccination must be at least 21 days old at time of entry (primary vaccination wait period)
- The vaccination must not be more than 12 months old at time of entry
- Vaccination must be recorded in the health certificate or EU pet passport

## Health Certificate
- For non-EU residents: an official health certificate issued by an accredited veterinarian is required
- The certificate must be issued within 10 days of the travel date
- For EU residents: the EU pet passport is accepted in place of a separate health certificate
- The certificate or passport must include: microchip number, owner details, vaccination dates, and tapeworm treatment record (for dogs)

## Tapeworm Treatment (Dogs Only)
- Required for dogs entering Turkey
- The treatment must be administered between 1 and 5 days before the date of entry — not earlier, not later
- The active ingredient must be praziquantel or an equivalent approved anthelmintic
- The treatment and date must be recorded by a veterinarian in the health certificate or pet passport

## Quarantine Rules
- No quarantine is required if all documentation is complete and valid
- If documentation is missing or incorrect, the animal may be held at the border until paperwork is resolved or returned to the country of origin at the owner's expense

## Number of Pets Per Person
- Passengers may import up to 5 pets per person without a commercial permit
- More than 5 pets requires a commercial import permit

## Airline Policies
Airline pet policies vary widely and are separate from government import regulations — both must be satisfied.
- **Turkish Airlines**: Allows small dogs and cats in the cabin (in an IATA-approved carrier, combined pet + carrier weight up to around 8 kg) on most routes to Turkey, in addition to checked-baggage and cargo options for larger pets.

- **Lufthansa**: Allows small pets in the cabin under the seat, subject to a combined weight limit of around 8 kg, on flights to Turkey. Larger pets travel as checked baggage.
- **Pegasus Airlines**: Allows small pets in the cabin on many routes, subject to carrier size and weight limits; advance notice and booking a pet spot is required as cabin space for pets is limited per flight.
- Always confirm the current cabin/cargo policy, carrier size limits, and any advance booking requirements directly with the airline — policies can change and may differ by route.

## Important Warnings
- The tapeworm treatment timing is strict — 1 to 5 days before entry. A treatment given 6 days before is non-compliant
- Book your vet appointment carefully to hit the 1–5 day window relative to your flight date
- Non-EU residents should ensure their health certificate is endorsed by their national authority if required

## Sources
- Turkish Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (TAGEM)
- EU pet travel rules (applicable as reference standard)
